September 21, 2026

Networks suspend White House pool coverage after Trump bars three outlets

tags: politics, media
sources: @groundnews

The White House revoked press access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after accusing them of publishing "fake news," and has threatened further bans. The television pool covering presidential events was suspended Monday after CNN, scheduled to handle that day's pool duty and share footage with ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News, was prevented from carrying out the assignment; the five networks said no replacement pool would be arranged and issued a joint statement saying no administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting. Barack Obama criticized the move in a speech at Colgate University, saying he could not imagine having barred Fox News during his own presidency. He added that roughly 30 to 35 percent of the country finding the step acceptable shows a gap in public understanding of what democracy requires.

All 50 states to join Medicaid drug pricing model, Trump says

tags: health, politics
sources: @groundnews

President Donald Trump announced that every state will participate in a Medicaid program applying Most Favored Nation pricing to selected prescription drugs, aligning their cost with what other wealthy countries pay. The program, called the Medicaid "GENEROUS" model, is part of broader drug pricing agreements the White House estimates could save $529 billion over ten years, though experts say the figure cannot be independently verified because the agreements with pharmaceutical companies have not been released. Because Medicaid patients already pay small copays, much of the savings would accrue to state Medicaid programs, which Trump said could reinvest the money in other health care improvements.

Pentagon hosts Logan and Jake Paul to address service members

tags: defence, politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos, @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department brought influencers Logan and Jake Paul to the Pentagon, where they toured the building and delivered remarks thanking service members and describing those willing to fight and die for the country as etching their names in history. Footage of the visit, which included a meeting with Pete Hegseth, was posted on the Pentagon's official page. The visit drew criticism across the political spectrum for taking place while American troops are deployed amid the war in Iran, with critics calling it an inappropriate use of the Pentagon during wartime and arguing it was aimed at selling the conflict to the public.

Push to criminalize criticism of Israel draws free speech objections

tags: politics, legal, privacy
sources: @ericmoutsos

Republican Representative Mike Lawler of New York, who has said anti-Israel chanting on college campuses is hate speech rather than protected expression, co-sponsored legislation with Democrat Josh Gottheimer to write the IHRA definition of antisemitism into federal law. Critics note that seven of the definition's eleven criteria concern criticism of the Israeli government, which would classify statements such as describing Israel's conduct in Gaza as genocide as a hate crime; the bill did not pass. Former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley has separately called for social media companies to disclose their algorithms and for every account to be verified under its user's real name, framing anonymous accounts and foreign bot networks as a national security threat. Opponents argue that ending online anonymity would expose people who criticize Israel to retaliation and that the First Amendment bars punishing people for stating what they believe to be true.

Obama calls for federal AI safeguards as administration resists regulation

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews

Speaking at Colgate University, Barack Obama argued that the federal government needs a regulatory framework for artificial intelligence as the technology advances, rejecting the claim from a senior Trump adviser that market incentives and liability risk will resolve safety issues on their own. He compared the argument unfavorably to the treatment of airlines, drug companies and food producers, saying 150 years of experience shows markets do not self-regulate where health and safety are at stake. Obama said the current administration is unwilling and unable to build such a framework, leaving a gap of at least a couple of years, and that voluntary restraint by leading AI companies should be encouraged in the interim as a stopgap rather than a substitute for rules.

Fifth Circuit strikes down federal limits on interstate handgun purchases

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Friday that federal restrictions on buying handguns directly across state lines are unconstitutional. The decision removes a long-standing requirement governing how handgun sales to out-of-state buyers may be conducted.

Trump signs orders expanding hunting and fishing on federal lands

tags: environment, politics
sources: @groundnews

President Trump signed two executive orders broadening access for hunters and anglers on federal lands and waters. One directs Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to open more federal land to hunting and fishing and rolls back Biden-era restrictions on lead ammunition and fishing tackle; the second expands fishing seasons and quotas and eases restrictions on boaters and anglers. Trump said public lands belong to the American people and pointed to the 2020 Great American Outdoors Act, which funded national park maintenance and the Land and Water Conservation Fund, saying a "2.0" version of that law would follow in the near future.

FAA to deploy AI traffic management system at Washington-area airports

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews

The Federal Aviation Administration plans to begin using an artificial intelligence traffic-management platform called SMART at Reagan National, Dulles International and Baltimore/Washington International as soon as Monday. The system analyzes schedules, weather and airport conditions to predict congestion and routing conflicts, and the FAA says it is designed to support rather than replace air traffic controllers while reducing delays and increasing airspace capacity. The rollout follows a June contract with Washington-based Air Space Intelligence. Reagan's main runway is the nation's busiest and the airport was the site of a January 2025 midair collision that killed everyone aboard both aircraft.

Resurfaced Salazar interview circulates as she breaks with Trump on immigration

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

An interview in which Republican Representative Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida was pressed by journalist Jim DeFede over her voting record is drawing renewed attention. Asked about publicizing funds for small businesses at Florida International University that came from the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023, which she voted against, she said she needed more details and would have to consult her staff, and repeatedly redirected to the $40 million she says she has brought to her district. DeFede also noted she voted against the CHIPS and Science Act while praising a climate resilience tech hub it funds in Miami, and against the infrastructure bill while citing airport funding. The interview is not new but has spread after Salazar broke with President Trump to urge him to change course on immigration policy.

Barksdale Air Force Base locked down twice in one day

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Barksdale Air Force Base was placed on lockdown twice in a single day following an active shooter incident. One lockdown followed a shooting victim gaining unauthorized access to the installation.
